title: Yo habría hecho lo mismo
blurbEn: What you would have done, in a past that never happened. The tense of hindsight and regret.
body:
Mi hermana discutió con su compañera de piso por una tontería enorme —el turno de la basura— y se fue de Sevilla dos días antes.

—¿Habrías hecho lo mismo? —me pregunta.

Yo habría aguantado. Habría dicho que no pasa nada, habría sonreído y habría vuelto a casa el domingo, como estaba previsto. Y después habría estado enfadada tres semanas sin decírselo a nadie. Habría escrito un mensaje larguísimo y no lo habría enviado.

Así que no: yo no habría hecho lo mismo. Yo habría hecho algo peor.

Se lo digo y se ríe.

—Deberías enfadarte más a menudo —me dice.

Puede que tenga razón. Enfadarse a tiempo es una habilidad que nadie me enseñó.

Ella lo hace sin esfuerzo. Es un talento raro y me da envidia.

Yo pido perdón cuando alguien me pisa el pie.
translationEn:
My sister argued with her flatmate over something enormous — whose turn it was to take out the rubbish — and left Seville two days early.

"Would you have done the same?" she asks me.

I would have put up with it. I would have said it didn't matter, I would have smiled and I would have gone home on Sunday, as planned. And then I would have been angry for three weeks without telling anyone. I would have written an enormously long message and not sent it.

So no: I wouldn't have done the same. I would have done something worse.

I tell her and she laughs.

"You should get angry more often," she says.

She may be right. Getting angry in time is a skill nobody taught me.

She does it effortlessly. It's a rare talent and I envy it.

I apologise when somebody steps on my foot.

habría.note: The conditional of 'haber' plus a participle. For a past that did not happen.

Deberías.note: 'deber' in the conditional is the standard way to give advice — softer than a command.

phrases.gloss: I would have put up with it

phrases.note: Like 'me da rabia' — the feeling is the subject and you are the object.
